title: climate focus europe wildfires hit tourist regions 2026 08 14
text:
LONDON, Aug 14 (Reuters) - Hello!
Wildfires hit parts of Croatia, Germany, France and Greece this week, prompting evacuations and injuries in tourist towns at the peak of the holiday season.
Hot weather and drought that scientists link to climate change have created ideal conditions for wildfires across Europe, especially in France, Spain and Greece. The Balkans have also endured several heatwaves.
A wildfire in Croatia descended on the tourist town of Omis overnight, engulfing houses, ​forcing about 1,000 people to evacuate to emergency shelters which opened in several towns on the stretch from Omis to Split, fire brigade and health officials said on Friday.
Around 36 ‌people were treated by ambulance services in the city of Split, about 25 km (15.5 miles) to the north, 14 were hospitalized and seven had life-threatening injuries, health officials said.
Meanwhile, more than 2,000 people evacuated their homes in western Germany on Friday, after a wildfire near the Belgian border spread towards a village, local authorities said.
Additionally, French authorities have evacuated 525 people from the village of Luglon after a wildfire broke out in the southwestern Landes region, not far from an area already devastated by major blazes ​this summer.
Luglon is about 100 km (62 miles) southeast of the tourist area of Arcachon Bay, where two major wildfires destroyed more than 50,000 hectares (124,000 acres), spurring the evacuation of as many as 220,000 ​people in late July.
In Greece, hundreds of holidaymakers fled a beach town in the northern region of Halkidiki on Thursday as a wildfire raced towards the shore.

Climate Buzz
A spring water resource that served as a lifeline for the nearby Palestinian village of Fasayil in the fertile Jordan Valley has been seized by Israeli settlers who channeled the ​water to an ancient pool in an archaeological site in the West Bank. Soon after, settlers advertised it as an Israeli tourist attraction and Israel's far-right finance minister pledged financial support. Click here for the full Reuters story.
During one of Japan's busiest holiday weeks, more than 360 mm (14 inches) of rain fell in 24 hours in parts of the Chiba area adjoining Tokyo, inundating roads and railways, with soldiers sent to help with rescue efforts. ​The record rainfall left thousands of travellers at Tokyo's Narita airport stranded on Friday, bringing floods to the surrounding area that disrupted transport, knocked out power to 20,000 homes and killed eight people.
Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez has called on the nation’s residents to conserve power and water less than two months after devastating twin earthquakes left more than 6,000 dead. El Niño was already ‌hitting the ⁠OPEC country and could bring drought before year-end. Click here to read more about the water and energy saving measures.
Just days after a powerful earthquake rocked Colombia’s third-largest city, Cali, crews have turned their attention from a search-and-rescue effort to debris removal at most sites, a sign the disaster response was entering a grimmer phase after the crucial first 72 hours.
Weather forecaster AccuWeather said in a statement that rounds of severe thunderstorms have been threatening the Plains, Midwest and East with damaging wind gusts and repeated downpours that triggered dangerous flash flooding. ​Power supply was cut on Thursday to about 540,000 ​homes and businesses across the U.S. Midwest as ⁠severe storms battered the region, data from PowerOutage.us showed.

Climate Commentary
Climate Lens
Indonesia is facing a longer and more severe dry season this year as El Nino intensifies, raising the risk of ⁠drought, forest fires ​and air pollution. Forestry Ministry data showed that 107,465 hectares (265,552 acres) of land were hit by fires from January to June, a ​110% increase compared with the same period in 2023, when El Nino last affected Indonesia. The figure is the highest ​rate in two decades, leading to six deaths and dozens of injuries this year, federal data showed, a grim count during a record-setting fire season in the United States.
